Let me work through this form completion.

Reporter: Daniel O'Connor (from the "From:" line and signature).
Subject: Wei Zhang.
DOB: 25/08/1992 → 1992-08-25.
Incident date: 9 March 2025 → 2025-03-09.
Incident time: 9:05 am → 09:05.
Phone: +61 3 9123 4567 → E.164: +61 followed by 9 digits. The number is 03 9123 4567. Normalising: drop the leading 0 of the area code, so +61 3 9123 4567 → +61391234567. That's +61 followed by 391234567 which is 9 digits. Good.
Site: "plant room, Level B2" — the subject line says "plant room B2". The document says "the plant room, Level B2". Site should be as named in the document, at most 60 chars. "Plant room, Level B2" — I'll use "plant room, Level B2" or "Plant room, Level B2". Let me use "Plant room, Level B2".
Severity: hospital treatment → high.
Injury reported: splash on forearm — is that an injury? The document reports a splash; she was taken to hospital for assessment. The instruction says injury_reported is true when the document reports any injury to the subject. A chemical splash on the forearm — the document says "was splashed on the forearm". It doesn't explicitly say injury, but severity rule says "any injury means at least medium, and hospital treatment means high." Hospital treatment means high regardless. Is a splash an injury? Hmm. The document says she was splashed with cleaning concentrate and taken to hospital for assessment. I'd say injury reported = true, since a chemical splash causing hospital assessment implies harm/injury. The severity is high due to hospital treatment. The injury_reported: the document reports a splash on the forearm — that's a physical contact with chemical, treated as injury. I'll say true.

Actually, let me consider: "injury_reported is true when the document reports any injury to the subject, otherwise false." The document doesn't explicitly say "injury" but describes a chemical splash on the forearm requiring hospital assessment. This is reasonably an injury (chemical burn potential). I'll mark true.

Summary: in the reporter's own words, at most 200 chars. The document gives: "In my words: Wei got a splash of concentrate on the forearm while swapping a drum and we sent her to hospital to be safe." That's the reporter's own words. Use that.

Count characters: "Wei got a splash of concentrate on the forearm while swapping a drum and we sent her to hospital to be safe." — that's well under 200.

variant.input_document:
From: Daniel O'Connor
To: WHS Team
Subject: Chemical splash, plant room B2

At 9:05 am on 9 March 2025 Wei Zhang (DOB 25/08/1992) was splashed on the forearm with cleaning concentrate while changing a drum in the plant room, Level B2. Wei was taken to hospital for assessment. In my words: Wei got a splash of concentrate on the forearm while swapping a drum and we sent her to hospital to be safe.

Daniel O'Connor, +61 3 9123 4567
variant.instructions:
# Incident report form: completion instructions

Read the case document and complete the form.

1. Output a single JSON object containing exactly the keys defined by the form schema, and no other text.
2. `reporter_name` is the full name of the person who made the report, exactly as written in the document.
3. `subject_name` is the full name of the person the incident happened to, exactly as written in the document.
4. `date_of_birth` is the subject's date of birth in ISO 8601 format YYYY-MM-DD.
5. `incident_date` is the date of the incident in ISO 8601 format YYYY-MM-DD.
6. `incident_time` is the 24-hour time HH:MM at which the incident occurred; omit this key entirely when the document states no time.
7. `phone` is the reporter's contact number normalised to E.164 with the +61 country code and no spaces or punctuation.
8. `site` is the place where the incident occurred as named in the document, in at most 60 characters.
9. `severity` is one of low, medium, or high: any injury means at least medium, and hospital treatment means high.
10. `injury_reported` is true when the document reports any injury to the subject, otherwise false.
11. `summary` restates what happened in the reporter's own words, in at most 200 characters.
